gaps: Primary source for every record: Bennett & Verspoor, British Columbia Executive Council Appointments 1871-1986 (LLBC, 1989), Appointments by Government pp.15-30 (PDF pp.16-31) and Appointments by Portfolio 1871-1903 pp.103-106 (PDF pp.104-107). Wikipedia ministry articles (source_secondary) are derived from it; where they differ, LLBC is used.

Wikipedia discrepancies noted: Elliott Minister of Mines start (Wikipedia 1 Feb 1876 vs LLBC 23 Feb 1876); Humphreys Mines 1878 (Wikipedia 11 Jul vs LLBC 13 Jul); Smithe ministry table on Wikipedia mis-dates Duck's end (1887) and Robson's second Finance term; Robson ministry Wikipedia start for Pooley/T. Davie 3 Aug 1889 matches LLBC.

Portfolio titles: LLBC lists short forms ('Lands and Works', 'Finance and Agriculture', 'Mines', 'Education and Immigration'); full styles used here follow LLBC's introduction and Wikipedia (Chief Commissioner of Lands and Works; Minister of ...). 'Attorney-General' hyphenated as in LLBC.
Party: pre-1903 governments were non-partisan (Wikipedia infoboxes: 'Non-partisan'); no individual party labels recorded.

LLBC ends every appointment at the premier's departure; holders who carried a portfolio into the next ministry are split per ministry and flagged retained_from_previous_ministry (LLBC asterisk). In 1874 (De Cosmos->Walkem) and 1887 (Smithe->A.E.B. Davie) and 1889 (A.E.B. Davie->Robson) ministers were not resworn; gaps of 1-4 days between ministries are genuine LLBC dates.

Vacancies (LLBC, some queried): President of the Council 11 Feb 1874-26 Oct 1875 [vacant?]; Mines 1-23 Feb 1876, 8 Aug-23 Oct 1877, 26 Jun-13 Jul 1878 [vacant?]; Provincial Secretary 8 Aug-23 Oct 1877 [vacant?]; President of the Council 13-16 Apr 1889; Attorney-General 27 Jul-7 Aug 1899; Education 28 Feb-12 Mar 1900 [vacant?].

President of the Council in the Joseph Martin ministry (28 Feb-14 Jun 1900) is given only as '[J. Martin?]' in LLBC; not recorded. Under Semlin, Semlin signed as 'Presiding Member' until mid-Sep 1898. Before 1899 the presidency was not a statutory portfolio and early holders are uncertain.

Omitted by design: Members/Ministers without Portfolio (Holbrook 15 Jan-26 Apr 1872; Armstrong 23 Dec 1872-28 Feb 1873; Theodore Davie 7 Jan-18 Jun 1888; McKechnie 17 Aug 1898-27 Feb 1900) and acting premierships (Walkem during De Cosmos's absences 1873-74; Robson [27] Jan-[28] Apr 1888). LLBC itself excludes most short acting appointments for ministers temporarily absent from Victoria, so acting coverage is incomplete.
Interim ministry (17 Aug-13 Nov 1871, no premier) included with premier=null for timeline completeness.
Prior's acting Chief Commissioner of Lands and Works (24 Oct-early Dec 1902) comes from a footnote only; end month approximate and it overlaps Wells's substantive tenure.
